Dar-Leanos and its surroundings

These lands are almost all Kania has left, and even holding them is uncertain. Undead attack the city, pests infest the fields and bandits roam the woods. However high its walls, the city's fall seems only a matter of time.

Return to Jigran and Dar-Leanos

The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where Baron Virril questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son Dartas and the overworked Master Stark. Stark provides a password for Uncle Rad, a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

Jaminin’s experiment and the undead

The trail of the local undead leads to Jaminin on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. [8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]

Weapons, Dartas and preparations for war

Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. [15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21]
